title: Eid al-Fitr: the day
hook: ghusl, perfume, best clothes, eating before prayer, a different road back (Bukhari)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the last ten nights of Ramadan, and the Prophet tightening his belt and waking his family. Your line was tighten the belt. Did you wake for one night, or part of one? Now the month is over. Day one thousand three hundred sixty-two.

A small detail, tucked into Sahih al-Bukhari, in a report from Jabir. On the day of Eid, the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, went out to the prayer by one road, and came home by another. That's the whole report. No reason given. Just two roads. Before that walk, there's a morning to get through: water, clothes, something sweet to eat. And after it, a walk home that doesn't retrace a single step. Today, the morning of Eid al-Fitr, the feast that breaks the fast, taken one small act at a time, the way the reports give it.
screen: `ONE ROAD OUT.` → `ANOTHER ROAD BACK.` → `NO REASON GIVEN.`

segments.voice: Start with water. In the Muwatta of Imam Malik, there's a report that Ibn 'Umar, a companion of the Prophet, would take a full bath, a ghusl, on the morning of the Fitr before going out to the prayer. The day begins clean. Then clothes. Al-Bukhari keeps a story in which 'Umar finds a fine cloak in the market and brings it to the Prophet, saying, in paraphrase: buy this, and dress up in it for Eid and for receiving visitors. The Prophet turned that one down, because it was silk. But notice what 'Umar took for granted: Eid is a day you dress for. For some, a little perfume too. Then food, and this is the surprise. After a month of not eating until sunset, the first act of the morning is to eat. Anas reports in al-Bukhari that the Prophet would not go out on the day of the Fitr until he had eaten some dates, and he ate them in an odd number. For a month, every fast broke at sunset. This one breaks in daylight, on purpose, before the prayer. Then the prayer itself, together with everyone. And then the road home, the different one. Why? Scholars have offered reasons: so that both roads see the people of the day, so that more neighbors get greeted, so that more ground bears witness to the prayer. But Jabir only tells us what he did. The meaning is left open, and the second road is still there to walk.
screen: `WATER: A GHUSL BEFORE GOING OUT.` · `CLOTHES: A DAY YOU DRESS FOR.` · `DATES BEFORE THE PRAYER.` · `A DIFFERENT ROAD HOME.`

segments.voice: The practice: walk a different way home. Settle, and breathe. First, in your mind, trace the way you usually come home: the turns, the corners, the same doors you pass every day. See how little of it you notice anymore. Now find one other way. One street over. The long way round the park. A different staircase. Just picture it, and picture who might be on that road whom you never pass. If you pray, you can keep in mind the Eid morning walk. If you don't, simply keep the new road ready for later. The bell holds the time.
Eid al-Fitr. The feast that breaks the fast of Ramadan: a bath, good clothes, dates before the prayer, and a different road back. Today's word.
Your line: a new road home. Today, take one route you don't usually take, and greet one person you meet on it. Tomorrow, Dhul Qa'dah. Day one thousand three hundred sixty-two.

howItsDone: On the morning of Eid al-Fitr, Muslims often bathe, put on their best clothes, eat a few dates, and go to the Eid prayer together, and some take a different road home afterward, following a report in Sahih al-Bukhari.

fork.setup: it's Eid morning, after a month of fasting till sunset. the prayer is soon. what does the Prophet do first, according to Anas?
options: keep fasting until after the prayer.
eat some dates before going out.
wait to eat until he's home again.
fork.reveal: he ate some dates, in an odd number, before going out. after a month of fasts broken at sunset, this one breaks in daylight, on purpose.

original.note: Arabic: the name of the feast at the end of Ramadan.

trapdoor: what you thought: Eid is the party after Ramadan.
what it means: a morning with a shape: a bath, good clothes, dates before the prayer, the prayer together, and a different road home.
what a scholar hears: Ibn 'Umar's ghusl in the Muwatta, Anas on the dates and Jabir on the two roads in al-Bukhari, with the reason for the roads left unstated.

sources.ref: Sahih al-Bukhari 986 (Jabir: on the day of Eid the Prophet took a different road back)

notes: Confirm hadith numbers: Bukhari 986, 953, 948; and the Muwatta reference for Ibn 'Umar's ghusl.
Perfume is in the outline hook but no report is cited for it; the script says only 'for some, a little perfume too'. A Keeper may add a source or cut it.
The reasons offered for the different road are given as 'scholars have offered reasons'; confirm these are fairly represented (e.g., from Ibn Hajar's commentary in Fath al-Bari).
'Out in the open' for the Eid prayer: the Prophet's practice was at the musalla; many communities today pray in mosques or halls. Confirm the phrasing.
